N.note: Bornaviral nucleocapsid protein (called the nucleoprotein, N, in this family), the 38/39 kDa doublet that is the most abundant protein in infected cells and >=50% of virion protein; the 39 kDa form carries an N-terminal PKRR nuclear localization signal (PMID 9188580) and assembles the polymerase complex with P and L (PMID 15992626). The 38 kDa alternative-initiation isoform is not modelled -- see notes/LITERATURE.md.

X.note: Non-structural X protein (p10), encoded by an ORF overlapping the 5' end of P. A negative regulator of polymerase activity (PMID 15992626); carries an unusual importin-alpha binding motif directing nuclear import (PMID 11796712); interferes with type I interferon signalling (PMID 23100370) and is controlled by Hsc70 (PMID 19397879).

P.note: Phosphoprotein p24, the polymerase cofactor and the central regulatory element directing assembly of the polymerase complex (PMID 15992626); phosphorylated by protein kinase C epsilon and casein kinase II (PMID 9268312).

M.note: Matrix protein; the crystal structure shows a tetramer with single-stranded RNA binding properties (PMID 19237566).

G.note: Envelope glycoprotein precursor p57, N-glycosylated to gp94, cleaved by furin into an N-terminal and a C-terminal subunit (PMID 9557754). Required for entry (PMID 9420287), for dissemination in neurons (PMID 14581559) and for cell-to-cell spread (PMID 26332529).

G_N.note: Mature N-terminal subunit of the glycoprotein, GP-N or GP1: the furin product with its signal peptide removed, residues 20-249 of the 503 aa BoDV-1 precursor. Richt 1998 places the furin cut after Arg249 (PMID 9557754) and the signal peptide is predicted here with SignalP 6.0; the resulting 230 aa agrees with the 27 kDa deglycosylated GP-N that Kiermayer 2002 finally detected in infected cells (PMID 12417322). Derived by locating the single R-X-[K/R]-R site in the window and extending through the basic run: P1=Arg in 150/150 members of the precursor collection, P1'=Asp in 149/150.

G_C.note: C-terminal furin cleavage product of the glycoprotein precursor, residues 250-503 of the 503 aa BoDV-1 protein (PMID 9557754); it carries the transmembrane anchor and runs to the precursor's own stop codon, so downstream_ext is 1 and only the N-terminus is a cleaved end.

L.note: The 190 kDa polymerase, nuclear, phosphorylated and bound to P (PMID 10756058). In Orthobornavirus the product depends on a splicing event that fuses a short upstream ORF in frame with the long downstream ORF (PMID 10756058); measured here, that first exon contributes only 5-6 residues (MSFHA/MSFHAR) and L is collinear in Carbovirus, Cultervirus and Cartilovirus. See notes/LITERATURE.md.

VP1.note: Cartilovirus only. Little skate bornavirus Vp1, an ancient duplication of the glycoprotein gene sharing G's N-terminus but lacking its transmembrane domain, with a predicted furin cleavage site (PMID 38028148). No function has been demonstrated, so the uncharacterized annotation is used and the designation is kept in the gene symbol. The symbol is written Vp1, as the describing paper writes it, to keep it distinct from the picornavirus and parvovirus capsid proteins called VP1.

VP2.note: Cartilovirus only. Little skate bornavirus Vp2, a second duplication sharing only the central region of the glycoprotein, 44% identical to Vp1 (PMID 38028148). No function demonstrated. The symbol is written Vp2, as the describing paper writes it, to keep it distinct from the parvovirus capsid protein called VP2.

N_PRIME.note: The p38 isoform of the nucleocapsid protein, called N' in the literature. It is translated from the second in-frame AUG, 13 residues into p40, and therefore lacks the PKRR nuclear localization signal that keeps p40 in the nucleus; p40 is nuclear and p38 is nuclear and cytoplasmic (PMID 9188580), and p38 is almost inactive in the polymerase complex, buffering the N:P ratio (PMID 15221540). Kojima 2019 uses the N / N' names explicitly and locates the second initiation codon at Met14 (PMID 30541858). Derived here by cutting each N collection member at its own second in-frame Met where that Met lies within the first 25 residues: 114 of 129 members qualify, at residue 14 in 69, 16 in 23 and 8 in 12. upstream_ext is 0 because scanning to a Met would walk back to p40's own start.

G_SP.note: The glycoprotein's N-terminal signal peptide, predicted with SignalP 6.0 (fast mode, eukarya) on one consensus N-terminus per G cluster and applied to the cluster's members. Six of seven clusters predict a signal peptide at probability 0.80-0.97 with cleavage after residue 19-25; the first mature residue is the modal residue in 98-100% of each cluster's members. A seventh cluster was withheld because its profile recalls its own training sequences at only 20.5 bits, below the 30-bit floor a caller would need. Removing it leaves the mature N-terminal subunit at 221-230 aa, and 230 for BoDV-1 -- about 27 kDa deglycosylated, which is what Kiermayer 2002 measured for GP-N (PMID 12417322).
